The implementation is complete: 22 files, ~3,300 lines, no dependencies, no package.json/node_modules. Here's a summary.

## Summary

I built a complete RS274/NGC G-code simulator in `output/` (entry point `output/main.js`, plain Node.js/CommonJS, zero dependencies). It implements the full language: expression evaluation, all G-codes (motion, arcs, canned cycles G81–G89, cutter radius compensation, coordinate systems, units, tool length offsets), all M-codes, tool-file and parameter-file I/O, straight-probing against a probe box, and the full trace-file format with time/distance/tolerance-based stepping.

**Validation performed** (all passing): the spec's own worked examples — Appendix C.1 (hello-world), C.2 (expression tests, all ~40 values verified exact), C.3 (canned cycles across all three planes), the G81 examples in §3.5.16.2 (positions and durations verified by hand to 9 decimal places), the G92 example in §3.5.18, and all three trace-format examples in the task spec (byte-for-byte structural match) — plus custom tests for G28/G30, probing (trip and non-trip cases), block-delete, parameter round-tripping, tool-file parsing, units conversion, helical arcs, and ~25 documented error conditions.

**Bugs found and fixed via testing** (not just spec-reading):
- P/Q are sticky across repeated canned-cycle lines — proven by Appendix C.3's own example, which my first draft rejected.
- Cutter radius compensation had two real geometry bugs: omitted axis words on a continuation line were resolving against the tool's offset position instead of the programmed contour, and the corner-arc convexity check assumed an invariant that doesn't hold when the preceding segment was an arc. Both caused valid programs to be spuriously rejected.
- Trace floating-point noise: arc interpolation at the endpoint didn't exactly match the authoritative end-of-move position, causing phantom near-zero deltas.
- Two missing documented error checks (G28/G30 and probing while cutter comp is on).
